dedupe_keys.name: arehs opengeosys workflow 3d thermo hydro mechanical simulation of a deep geological repository under changing boundary conditions ufz and tu bergakademie freiberg

description: This Zenodo record holds the OpenGeoSys workflow built in the AREHS project, German for effects of changing boundary conditions on the development of hydrogeological systems, by Tobias Meisel, Florian Zill, Wenqing Wang and Lars Bilke of the Helmholtz Centre for Environmental Research with Christian Silbermann and Dominik Kern of TU Bergakademie Freiberg. It is the basis for 3D thermo-hydro-mechanical simulation of a deep geological repository with changing boundary conditions based on geological reference models, and defines every step from the geological and physical model through finite element runs in OpenGeoSys to the figures in the final report; the clay and salt results in the report were made with it. The page says the framework is modular and highly parameterised, lets users vary model properties, processes and meshing, and has a generic SLURM interface to high-performance computers such as JUWELS at the Julich Research Centre. Version 1.0 is a free download of about 1.1 GB under BSD-3-Clause, published in May 2024. Coverage is the project reference models for clay and salt host rock. Caveats: the record points to separate workflow documentation, and runs need HPC resources. Simulation uses are long-term host-rock response for radioactive waste repository safety under changing climate boundary conditions. Related records: model-cyclus-nuclear-fuel-cycle-simulator covers the nuclear fuel cycle.
